import cv2, numpy as np

# Let's inspect obs_0040.png for the floor lamp base contact
img = cv2.imread('/work/observations/obs_0040.png')
# Pose 40: x=1.0, y=3.8, heading=180.0 (facing -y)
# Floor lamp base:
# Find pixels of the base of the lamp
# The base is dark grey ellipse/cylinder
hsv = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV)
# lamp base color in obs 40:
# Let's find grey pixels in lower-left region
# Base is around x in [50, 130], y in [380, 440]
crop = img[380:440, 50:130]
print('Obs 40 lamp base region min/max y:')
# Let's find lowest pixel of the lamp base
for r in range(439, 370, -1):
    row_pixels = img[r, 50:130]
    # check if any pixel is dark grey: R,G,B close to each other, around 70-120
    diff = np.abs(row_pixels[:,0].astype(int) - row_pixels[:,1].astype(int)) + np.abs(row_pixels[:,1].astype(int) - row_pixels[:,2].astype(int))
    grey = (diff < 10) & (row_pixels[:,0] > 60) & (row_pixels[:,0] < 130)
    if np.any(grey):
        cols = np.where(grey)[0] + 50
        print(f'Row {r}: cols {cols.min()} to {cols.max()}, center {(cols.min()+cols.max())/2}')
        break
